editorial.description_en: Wood ash mixed into sand — warm, but dark enough that the warmth reads as depth rather than as colour.
editorial.description_ja: 灰のまじった砂のような、くすんだ色。

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.606, C 0.012, h 72.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 灰 (hai, ash) + 砂 (suna, sand). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Ash Sand" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 灰砂. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — fuyu-tsuchi at ΔE00 5.7, togi-ishi at ΔE00 8.2, asa-nawa at ΔE00 8.5. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.012 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
